newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may import power as plant output dwindles.
newsitem.headline: Poland may import power as plant output dwindles.

text.p: Poland could have to impose power cuts or import electricity if temperatures plunge below zero after a strike led to reduced output at the country's largest power plant, a senior power grid official said on Sunday.

The giant Belchatow plant, which produces electricity for about 25 percent of the country, has already cut output by two-thirds over the weekend because of a strike at the state-owned KWB Belchatow lignite mine, its sole fuel supplier.

"Even if the powerplant ground to a halt, we should have enough reserve power from other plants as long as temperatures remain above freezing," Stanislaw Poreba, deputy head of the Power Grid Company (PSE), told private Radio Zet.
"But if temperatures were to fall much below freezing, we might have to resort to imports and sporadic power shortages could occur." Poreba said.

Henryk Posmyk, head engineer on duty at the Belchatow plant, on Sunday said that dwindling coal supplies may soon force the plant to shut down two more power-generating blocks. "The striking miners have further reduced their coal supply and we could be forced to limit operations to only two out of 12 power blocks soon," Poskyk told Reuters.
On Friday workers at KWB Belchatow reduced coal deliveries to back demands for the dismissal of their director general after weeks of discussions yielded no results.

Late on Friday, the Treasury Ministry said in a statement that it was seriously considering the charges against the director and said that strikers would be responsible for any possible losses caused by halting coal supplies.
